Cardiomyopathies Cardiomyopathy is a term used to describe diseases of the heart muscle associated with cardiac dysfunction. Al- though formerly used to describe conditions with an unknown cause (idiopathic), increased awareness of dis- ease mechanisms and genetic factors has broadened the definition. Cardiomyopathies may develop as a conse- quence of other cardiovascular or systemic disorders, such as systemic or pulmonary hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, valvular heart disease, congenital abnormalities, metabolic disorders, inflammatory or infectious diseases, and drug-induced conditions. Primary cardiomyopathies (those affecting only or predominantly the heart muscle) have usually been divided into 3 distinct types namely di- lated cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and restrictive cardiomyopathy; the dilated and hypertrophic forms are the two major types.
